title: Graphs: DFS Traversal
oneLiner: Same graph, same start node as BFS -- but diving all the way down one path before backtracking produces a completely different visit order.
keyTakeaway: DFS on a graph is the same recursive shape as a PREORDER tree traversal (record the node, then recurse into its neighbors), plus the one addition every graph traversal needs that a tree never does: a VISITED set, since a graph (unlike a tree) can have cycles that would otherwise recurse forever.
explanation:
DFS explores as far as possible down one path before backtracking: recurse into a node, mark it visited, then recurse into its first unvisited neighbor, and that neighbor's first unvisited neighbor, and so on -- only backtracking (returning to try the NEXT neighbor) once a path runs out of new nodes to reach. That's the same recursive pattern as the tree DFS in Binary Trees: Inorder Traversal, but recording each node BEFORE its neighbors -- PREORDER. A graph node's neighbors have no left/right split, so there's no "inorder" slot between them. Graph DFS adds one thing a tree traversal never needed: the VISITED check. A tree has no cycles, so recursion naturally never revisits a node; a graph can (see Graphs: BFS Traversal for the cycle in this sample graph), so without checking "if visited, skip" before recursing, DFS on a cyclic graph recurses forever.

Compare this traversal's order against BFS's on the exact same graph, from the exact same start node (0): BFS fans out one whole ring of distance at a time; DFS commits to node 1's entire branch before ever coming back to try node 2 -- same graph, same starting point, genuinely different visit order. That's the concrete version of "BFS finds the shortest path first, DFS doesn't" -- DFS might stumble onto a long, winding path to a nearby node before ever trying the short direct edge, because it commits to a direction instead of looking around at every option first.

Try it below -- watch the current node's border light up, and the path back to the start (amber) shrink each time DFS backtracks.
